findings.what: The DeepCenter M1 gate code has two gaps against the pre-registered text. (a) t* = argmax of SELECTION delta over the NON-control arms only. The control 0.25 can never be t*, so the rule 'if t* = 0.25, no build' is unreachable: an arm worse than the control on SELECTION can still become t*. (b) With t* = 0.15 (grid edge) the plateau checks only one neighbour (0.20), so the strict reading that is in force passes with one neighbour. At t* = 0.20 it always fails, because the control neighbour has delta 0. The result is perverse: the most aggressive threshold is the only one the in-force gate can pass.
findings.evidence: tools/trainlab.py l.731-745 (arms_dc excludes DC_CONTROL; best = max(cands); neigh = grid[k-1], grid[k+1] if in range); DC_THRESHOLDS = (0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35); T9 text 'если t* = 0.25, сборки нет', '>= +0.001 при обоих соседних порогах'
findings.action: Before reading any exp60 number, add the AND clauses sel[t*] > 0 (else t* = control, no build) and len(neighbours) == 2 (a grid-edge t* has an unverifiable plateau, so no build under the strict reading). Record both in CONTEXT as a bug fix that only tightens the gate (no OK needed). Report the old and new verdicts side by side.

findings.what: The K3b verdict 'in force' (strict plateau AND L2) removes the ORIGINAL precision clause (TP / all new forks >= 0.35) and replaces it with the L2 evaluable precision TP/(TP+FP), which is always >= the original value. Example: 3 TP, 3 FP, 4 ignored new forks gives original 0.30 (fail) but evaluable 0.50 with Wilson lower bound 0.268 > 0.265 (pass). This loosens a pre-registered gate without the user's OK. v4 itself says anything that loosens a gate needs [OK].

findings.what: It is not written down how K3 is read if it bundles forkmid (C04, R3 class) with forkblob, which is R3 only after the user's OK and R4 before it (needs >= +0.002 on the LB). Under R3, a bundle at -0.002 closes BOTH riders forever. Under R4, a bundle at 0/+0.001 would still keep forkmid. Deciding this after the K3 score would be choosing the rule by the result.
findings.evidence: CONTEXT 13:38 R3/R4 text (C04 listed in R3); ADDENDUM L4 '[rule frozen now; R3 class needs OK]'; FINAL_REPORT_v4 slots 'S4: K3 = K2 + [forkmid] + [forkblob]'
findings.action: Before building K3, write into CONTEXT: (i) with no user OK on forkblob-as-R3 at build time, K3 = K2 + forkmid only (and only if the ORIGINAL T9 forkmid gate passes; L3 needs the OK). (ii) If both riders are bundled after the OK, the bundle is read by R3 as one rider, and a failure (<= -0.002) closes both. (iii) If neither passes its gate, S4 stays empty (no 'try anyway').
